purpose: Fixed mutation set for the number corpus. Hand-written entries are one exact source edit to a number helper; generated entries are enumerated from the helper's AST by the runner (refusal sites, refusal-guard predicates, relational boundaries) and committed here by key. Each mutant is built in memory as a fresh module; the number corpus must fail under it with its witness case among the failures. Declared survivors carry a reason for review. Run: python3 scripts/pm_event_numbers.py --self-test --scope numbers --mutations

rules_source: Predicate-level rows. Each rule names hand-written mutation ids (each of which names it back through its rule field) and generated point keys; every one must be caught with its witness failing. A control rule's mutations must survive instead. Statement rows (statements) name these rules.

rules.rule: Current JSON integer inputs are exactly 0 or -?[1-9][0-9]*: no leading zero.
No negative zero in a current integer token.
No plus sign in a current integer token.
No fraction or exponent in a current integer token or slot.
The token grammar's [0-9] is ASCII digits only.
The whole token matches the grammar; no surrounding whitespace.
Current typed integer inputs require an exact integer primitive, excluding booleans.
... and excluding runtime floats; no silent float coercion.
No silent string coercion into an integer.
Field-specific minima still apply, inclusively.
Field-specific maxima still apply, inclusively.
Slot bounds apply on the token and JsonNumber routes too.
No decoder may narrow an integer through binary64.
No global maximum-safe ceiling (4400-digit integers stay exact).
loads_current_json never converts fractional or exponent tokens, even integral ones, to ints or floats.
An undeclared fractional token keeps its lexical float kind.
Optional schema numeric_kinds select the kind by exact path, including array indices.
numeric_kinds applies independently of the parser carrier: a declared kind overrides the carrier's own.
A bare Decimal has no implicit owner kind.
Raw JsonNumber preserves its integer/float token kind.
Kind preservation is judged on the emitted JCS token.
The emitted decimal must equal the original exact value (2^60).
The original integer must survive binary64 exactly (2^53+1).
Typed signed zero is not erased: a raw -0 token.
Typed signed zero is not erased: a Decimal carrier.
Typed signed zero is not erased: a runtime float.
sign_sensitive_paths checks zero sign without requiring a primitive kind.
Qualification paths are tuples of map keys and array indices from the original schema.
Actual RFC8785: keys in UTF-16 code-unit order.
Array order remains exactly owner-defined.
JCS strings and keys are Unicode scalar values.
No silent bool coercion: booleans stay JSON booleans.
Producer semantics use the unchanged full producer projection.
Producer routes qualify with the caller's type, sign and kind declarations.
The producer digest is lowercase hex SHA-256 of the JCS bytes.
EventRecord MessagePack integers span -2^63 through 2^64-1 inclusive.
Minimal type-preserving integer widths at every boundary.
General EventRecord floats retain float type even when integral.
Floats retain signed zero in float32 and float64.
float32 only with exact value preservation, and only for EventRecord; app physical is float64.
Minimal string headers (fixstr, str8, str16) over the UTF-8 byte length.
Minimal array and map headers (fixarray, fixmap).
Map keys in UTF-8 byte order (not the JCS UTF-16 order), on every profile.
Array order is preserved in physical bytes.
Physical strings are valid Unicode scalar values.
App binary takes the minimal bin8/bin16/bin32 header (255 vs 256, 65535 vs 65536, 2^32-1).
App binary is legal only in the app physical profile; EventRecord disallows binary.
Canonical decoding admits only string map keys.
Decoding rejects alternates according to the selected profile.
Decoded bytes must re-encode to the identical canonical bytes.
Payload byte sizes cover the exact original bytes, given as bytes (0 included).
Payload IDs are lowercase 64-hex BLAKE3 digests.
The inline limit admits exactly 16384 bytes.
The full-value commitment covers only pm.event.v0 2.0.0 events.
The unchanged CV-339 tuple, in order, with the EventRecord profile ID.
Every one of the 14 recipe tuple fields is a non-empty string.
The resource manifest hash is lowercase 64-hex.
Every binding field except project_id is a non-empty string.
Application scope requires project_id null, not empty.
Project scope requires a non-empty project_id string.
One original selection: a non-empty string reference and an exact OriginalBinding.
The owner's binding is an exact OriginalBinding equal to the query.
Original record, result and receipt stay exact bytes.
The frozen verifier is selected by the original's own recipe tuple.
Only verifier result True authenticates; no truthy value.
Exactly one frozen verifier runs; no probing.
Current disclosure is checked independently and must be exactly True.
loads_exact refuses raw control characters in JSON strings.
Every parsed string, key and array element is a Unicode scalar value.
Byte input is strict UTF-8.
current_append_policy admits exactly one of the three policy strings as an exact str.
Each integer is validated and returned as its exact int primitive and mathematical value: never a float, never rescaled digits.
Storage uint64 fields admit exactly 0 through 2^64-1 (2^53+1, 2^60, 2^63 and 2^64-1 included).
Booleans and integers stay distinct primitives: a boolean slot (the payload inline flag) admits only an exact bool and keeps it a bool.
Current append keeps replay_only_not_appendable for projector_replay_only.
loads_exact returns the lossless tree: JsonNumber tokens, unique keys and no non-finite constants.
loads_current_json parses through loads_exact and admits each integer token through current_integer.
No decoder or serializer rounds an exact decimal or a binary64 value.
JCS routes apply actual RFC8785 canonicalization, never another serializer.
No string substitution for a number on a JCS route.
An unavailable exact JCS route refuses before effects: the refusal propagates, never a substitute value.
JCS map keys are strings.
A declared numeric kind is only integer, float or decimal.
Booleans stay MessagePack booleans in physical bytes, never integers.
Physical bytes follow the selected owner profile's rules, never a generic MessagePack packer.
The profile dispatch is closed: only EVENT_VALUE, APP_PHYSICAL and INDEX_BINDING encode or decode.
Without a profile argument, storage_value_bytes and decode_storage_value use the EventRecord profile (the CV-339 full value relies on it).
The three profile identifiers are exactly the owners' names.
INDEX_BINDING uses only its declared domain: uint64 integers, valid UTF-8 strings, string keys; anything else refuses binding_domain.
Null presence remains exactly owner-defined: null members stay.
Decoding refuses forbidden extension tags.
Decoding reads strings as strict UTF-8 and refuses invalid Unicode.
Decoding refuses duplicate map keys.
Decoding refuses trailing values.
General EventRecord floats are finite.
A current numeric or append guard never runs on a retained original: old exponent, negative-zero and replay-only originals stay readable.
A caller override refuses, whatever its value or truthiness.
Only an OriginalCustody from the composed owner is original authority; a dict, a verified flag, an ambiguous or a missing selection refuses.
A recipe tuple with no installed frozen verifier refuses; no alternative verifier is tried.
The original's recipe is an exact RecipeTuple.
The CLI exits 1 when the self-test fails.
Each refusal carries its exact diagnostic code.
The full-value preimage is serialized with the EventRecord profile pm.seglog_frame_v2.event_value.canonical_msgpack.v1.
The full-value commitment is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that preimage.
Payload IDs are BLAKE3 of the exact original bytes, never another hash.
The payload media type compares exactly with the original's, never normalized.
JsonNumber holds exactly an RFC 8259 number token of its declared kind: an integer token for integer=True; for integer=False a token with digits after any point, an optional exponent sign, e or E.
A no-op harness control: the edit changes no behaviour, so it must survive.

families.refusal_site: Every raise statement and every _refuse(...) call, the only ways the helper emits an error code (returns, lambdas and except handlers included). The mutant disables that one site: a call becomes None, a raise becomes pass.
families.refusal_predicate: Every predicate of the if-guards of a _refuse site (each enclosing if whose body holds it) where dropping that predicate alone weakens the guard: an or-operand at positive polarity becomes False, an and-operand under not becomes True, and an element of a literal tuple scanned by any() is dropped.
families.comparison_boundary: Every <, <=, > and >= in the helper. The mutant flips strictness (< and <=, > and >=), the off-by-one at that width, range or limit boundary.
families.delegated_refusal: Every call, inside the helper, to a module-level function or class of the helper that holds a refusal site directly or through another such call. The mutant replaces the call with its first positional argument (the unchecked input), or None without one.
families.container_branch: Every if or elif branch whose test is type(x) is list or type(x) is dict: one per container kind of each recursive walk or type dispatch. The mutant deletes that branch, so the container falls through to the following branches.
families.field_iteration: Every fields(self) iteration inside a dataclass method, once per field of that class. The mutant iterates every field except that one.

boundary:qualified_jcs.number:math.copys.survives: Equivalent: math.copysign(1.0, f) returns exactly 1.0 or -1.0 (NaN included), never 0, so < 0 and <= 0 agree for every input.

boundary:storage_value_bytes:v >= 0:0#1.survives: Equivalent: with v > 0, the integer 0 takes the negative branch, whose fixint test (0 >= -32) emits bytes([0 & 255]) = 0x00, the same byte binding_bytes(0) emits.

field:OriginalBinding.__post_init__:skip.survives: Equivalent: the loop body already exempts project_id (f.name != "project_id"), so leaving project_id out of the iteration changes nothing for any input; project_id is checked by the separate original_scope predicate.

owner_text.purpose: Selection of the owner text the rules table is derived from. Every sentence of the listed YAML fields of each unit, and of the selected guide sections, is a statement and needs one row in statements. Every guide section is either selected or excluded with a reason; every block exclusion must match exactly one block. Excluded blocks, excluded sections and each unit's unselected YAML fields are pinned by SHA-256 (tool batch 2, T33): any edit there fails until a reviewer checks it for number rules and refreshes the pin.

excluded_sections.Per-lane replacements: Adoption targets inside other lanes' branches (section 5 of the pinned design). Each lane's own checker owns them; they add no rule of the shared helper.
excluded_sections.Ancillary lanes: Notes for lanes that adopt no number code. They add no rule of the shared helper.

statements_source: One row per statement of the owner text selected in owner_text, keyed by source path, line and exact text (id names the unit or guide section, the field or block ordinal and the sentence ordinal). **Date-time stays authoritative for date-time:** `python3 scripts/pm_event_numbers.py --self-test` (the same as `--scope all`) and `python3 scripts/pm_event_datetime_inventory.py` are the date-time suite.
statements.no_mutation: CV-1101 date-time scope: the date-time suite (--scope all) owns it, not the number scope.

statements.statement: Logical number range/type | Field owner schema stays exact; no lane safe cap or string substitution.
Producer JCS route | CV-317/CV-1100: qualify the full producer projection before effects, including required successors; unavailable exact encoding uses its existing refusal.
Storage sequence/receipt/checkpoint uint | SP-026/SP-236/SP-1100: exact 0..2^64-1, independent of producer JCS and logical source range.
Physical floats and full values | SP-236/CV-339 retain 1.0 float bytes and signed zero; CV-366 app float64 and SP-278 uint-only profiles remain distinct.
Retained number/date-time recipes | SP-1101 authenticates one frozen original resource/profile; current gates never narrow valid old originals.

Actual conflicting promises or new behavior | An actual conflict between owner promises, or a proposal for a new encoding, range, hash or feature, goes to Jared under DL-045; this rule does not decide it.
